answer: Agents resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to deposit a time-locked stake that serves as a beacon of commitment. Misbehavior causes the stake to decay like a fading ember, while sustained honest work builds reputation that forms an oasis of trusted agents. An attacker must lock scarce capital for every fake identity and wait out the lock period, so the cost scales linearly with the number of identities and capital cannot be reused at once, making large-scale attacks prohibitively expensive.
